_meta.indication: Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults; not indicated for preventive treatment of migraine

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group trial of two doses of lasmiditan (100 mg and 200 mg) compared to placebo in the acute treatment of migraine
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of migraine with and without aura per ICHD-II criteria; predominantly female (84%) and White (78%), mean age 42 years (range 18-81)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: proportion of patients pain-free at 2 hours and MBS-free at 2 hours after the initial dose
pivotal_trials.n: Randomized: REYVOW 100 mg n=744, 200 mg n=745, placebo n=742
pivotal_trials.result: Pain free at 2 hours: 100 mg 28.3%, 200 mg 31.8% vs placebo 15.3% (both p<0.001). MBS free at 2 hours: 100 mg 41.2%, 200 mg 40.7% vs placebo 29.6% (both p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel group trial of three doses of lasmiditan (50 mg, 100 mg and 200 mg) compared to placebo in the acute treatment of migraine
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of migraine with and without aura per ICHD-II criteria; predominantly female (84%) and White (78%), mean age 42 years (range 18-81)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: proportion of patients pain-free at 2 hours and MBS-free at 2 hours after the initial dose
pivotal_trials.n: Randomized: REYVOW 50 mg n=750, 100 mg n=754, 200 mg n=750, placebo n=751

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and > placebo) were dizziness, fatigue, paresthesia, and sedation; dizziness occurred in 9% (50 mg), 15% (100 mg), 17% (200 mg) vs 3% placebo. Serotonin syndrome was reported in lasmiditan-treated patients.
target_moa: Lasmiditan is a selective serotonin (5-HT) 1F receptor agonist that binds with high affinity to the 5-HT1F receptor; unlike triptans it does not target 5-HT1B/1D receptors

advisory_committee.vote: Application not referred to an advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, efficacy findings clear, and safety profile acceptable

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) for a new molecular entity received October 11, 2018 and approved October 11, 2019 on its PDUFA goal date; the first selective 5-HT1F receptor agonist reviewed by FDA, approved based on two adequate and well-controlled efficacy trials, without referral to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received October 11, 2018, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Reyvow (lasmiditan) 50 mg and 100 mg tablets.
Lasmiditan is a new molecular entity (NME) developed for the acute treatment of migraine with and without aura in adults.
The efficacy of lasmiditan was demonstrated in two adequate and well-controlled studies.

Your application for Reyvow was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for use in the intended population.
